anomalies.observed: The 10k pull-up R6 on the TACH net is tied to the global rail VCC (the unregulated input rail that feeds the LM1117-5.0 input pin and the high-side PMOS fan switch), while the same TACH net drives the MCU tachometer input pin2 (PB4) of U2/U3, whose VCC pin8 is on the regulated +5V rail.
anomalies.expected: A pull-up for a signal that is read by the ATtiny must be tied to the MCU's own supply (+5V), exactly as the RST pull-up R3 is correctly tied to +5V. Pulling TACH to VCC (which is necessarily higher than +5V, otherwise the 5V regulator could not function) places an over-voltage on the MCU input pin.

U2 ATtiny45-20P pin2 = 'TACH', pin8 = '+5V'; U3 ATtiny13V-10S pin2 = 'TACH', pin8 = '+5V' (sheet /, rows B/C)
RST pull-up R3 = 10K tied to '+5V' (correct rail), whereas R6 tied to 'VCC' (sheet /, row A)

anomalies.impact: When the fan tach transistor is off, the TACH line is pulled to VCC (e.g. 12V), exceeding the ATtiny pin absolute-maximum (VCC+0.5V) and the +5V rail; this risks damaging/latching-up the MCU input and gives a wrong logic level on the tachometer reading.
